summary: A low-key, self-guided evening graze through Chiang Mai's residential Santitham: browse the Thanin/Siriwattana covered market for prepared dishes, then look for the neighbourhood's grilled-food carts. It is an everyday local-food outing rather than a single night market with a fixed, guaranteed line-up. Make the most of it early, since the market's vendors can close before the street carts.
whyGo: See a working neighbourhood food scene with covered market counters and casual evening carts.
Sample a few small things—such as northern sausage, grilled pork, noodles or fruit—instead of committing to one large meal.
Get away from the Old City's main visitor circuits without travelling far from the north side of the moat.
bestFor: Independent travellers happy to browse, point and order in a Thai-language setting
People who enjoy grilled snacks and informal food stalls
A flexible dinner that can be shortened or extended based on what is open
skipIf: You need a fully mapped route with every stop guaranteed open on a specific weekday.
You need assured vegetarian, halal, gluten-free or allergen-controlled food without advance confirmation.
You require step-free, wheelchair-accessible paths and seating throughout.
duration: Allow 1.5–2.5 hours for a relaxed graze and short walks; this is a planning estimate. Leave more time if you are travelling across town.
cost: Plan on about THB 150–350 per person for several snacks or a casual meal, plus drinks and transport. This is a budget estimate: current menus and prices for the market and carts were not published in the sources checked. Carry small cash.
hours: A Chiang Mai street-food guide lists Thanin/Siriwattana Market as roughly 06:00–21:00 daily, with some vendors closing earlier. An individual grilled pork cart beside Seven Santitham is listed daily 16:00–01:00; a grilled-intestine vendor on Thewan Road is listed from 17:00 to around midnight. Listings can lag reality; arrive around 17:30–19:00 for the best overlap and check current hours locally.
bestTime: Go around 17:30–19:00, starting at Thanin/Siriwattana before its prepared-food counters wind down, then continue to evening grills. Sunday offers the option of comparing with the Old City's Sunday Walking Street, but that is a separate, much busier outing.
gettingThere: Set a map pin for Siriwattana/Thanin Market in Santitham and walk between nearby stops. From the Old City or Nimman, use a red songthaew or a ride-hailing car to the market; fares vary with route, demand and negotiation, so confirm before boarding. Cart listings give useful pins: the pork cart is beside Seven Santitham, while the grilled-intestine shop is at 55/3 Thewan Road. Use the precise pin rather than relying on transliterated street names.
booking: No booking is needed for markets or carts; these are walk-up stops. Message or call a specific cart only if its availability matters to your plan. Treat vendor availability and dishes as day-to-day rather than guaranteed.
accessibility: Step-free routes, accessible toilets, wheelchair clearance and seating at individual stalls were not verified. Expect market aisles, sidewalks and curbside carts to be busy or uneven, and many seats to be low stools. The area is residential and spread across small streets; use a car for the longer links if walking is difficult.
practicalTips: Start with a small portion at the market, then add one or two grilled snacks; stall selection and stock vary.
Choose food cooked to order and served hot; for raw produce, ice and water, use your own comfort level and prefer sealed drinking water.

Many classic northern and street-food dishes contain pork, fish sauce, shrimp paste, wheat, egg or shared cooking oil. Ask about ingredients directly; a meat-free-looking dish is not necessarily vegetarian or vegan.
Carry small baht notes and keep a translation of dietary restrictions ready. Some vendors may have limited English or no printed menu.
For a photo reference, the linked Santitham image is a representative market-food scene from a local lodging blog; it is not a claim about a particular stall on the route.
decemberNotes: December is generally a comfortable season for an outdoor evening walk, but no special December 2026 market schedule was found. Confirm holiday opening around Christmas and New Year, when individual vendors may take breaks. Darkness comes earlier than in summer; watch traffic while crossing and use a phone light on smaller sois.
uncertainties: The current configuration and evening opening of Thanin/Siriwattana's food counters were not confirmed with a market operator; the published hours come from a 2024 traveller guide.
Third-party business listings provide hours for two carts, but their menus, current prices and holiday schedules are unconfirmed.
The Sunday Soi 9 food-row detail appears in one recent neighbourhood guide but is not corroborated by an official listing; do not make the route depend on it.
Photo reuse permission is not established; the image is included as a credited linked reference.
